data.title: Keratolysis exfoliativa — viva
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Keratolysis exfoliativa** (Eczemas)_

**Q1. What is keratolysis exfoliativa?**
- Common benign recurrent superficial peeling of palms (and soles) — also called lamellar dyshidrosis/exfoliatio areata manuum
- Young adults; worse in summer, with sweating, friction, wet work, detergents

**Q2. Describe the clinical features.**
- Small air-filled white 'collarettes' or blisters (no fluid) that burst to leave expanding rings of peeling; leaves normal or slightly red, tender skin
- Usually asymptomatic or mild dryness; symmetrical palms > soles; no vesicles with fluid, no significant inflammation

**Q3. What causes it?**
- Premature separation of corneocytes in the stratum corneum — possibly reduced corneodesmosomes/protease imbalance; irritants, hyperhidrosis and seasonal factors aggravate; some link with atopy

**Q4. Classify palmoplantar eczema / differentials (PYQ).**
- Palmar eczema types: irritant, allergic, atopic, pompholyx (dyshidrotic), hyperkeratotic, nummular, fingertip, apron eczema, recurrent focal palmar peeling (= keratolysis exfoliativa)
- Differentials of peeling palms: pompholyx (deep fluid vesicles, itchy), tinea manuum (one hand, KOH +), psoriasis, acral peeling skin syndrome (TGM5 — genetic, from birth, worse with friction), post-scarlet fever/Kawasaki/TSS desquamation, epidermolysis bullosa simplex (localised), juvenile plantar dermatosis, secondary syphilis

**Q5. Investigations?**
- Clinical diagnosis; KOH to exclude tinea; patch test if associated eczema

**Q6. Treatment.**
- Reassurance; avoid soaps, detergents, irritants and wet work; gloves
- Emollients and keratolytic/humectant creams (urea 10–20%, lactic acid 12%, salicylic acid 3–6%); barrier creams
- Topical steroids usually not useful (non-inflammatory) unless eczematous; NB-UVB in extensive recurrent cases; treat hyperhidrosis

**Q7. Differentiate keratolysis exfoliativa from pompholyx.**
- KE: air-filled superficial collarettes, minimal itch, no fluid vesicles, non-inflammatory
- Pompholyx: deep-seated tapioca-like fluid-filled vesicles on sides of fingers, intense itching, inflammatory, responds to steroids

**Q8. Prognosis?**
- Benign, recurrent each summer; tends to resolve on its own in 2–3 weeks per episode

## Quick spotter facts
- Air-filled collarettes on palms in summer — keratolysis exfoliativa

_Sources: Previous-year PG question papers (Sahana P Raju, Solved Papers Dermatology); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e (Palmoplantar dermatoses). Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
